text:
Samir Patel: Heads up — we triggered an anomaly on KMS decrypt rates for key `redwood-prod-01` in us-west-2. We rotated the key and revoked the implicated service account token. No confirmed exfiltration so far, but we need an exec update and a customer advisory draft. @Jordan (CPO) @Leah can you help with comms?

Incident Bot: ALERT 03:21 UTC — KMS anomaly detector: high decrypt rate (key redwood-prod-01). Alert ID: kb-2024-9032.

Leah Gomez: Thanks Samir. Can you paste the short timeline + impacted surface? I can sketch a customer note. Prefer conservative language ("no evidence to date").

Samir Patel: Timeline: 02:58 UTC — detector spike; 03:03 — identified service-account (svc-ingest-usw2); 03:07 — rotated key + revoked SA token; 03:20 — additional traffic suppressed. Impact: internal service traffic only, we see no external egress to unfamiliar IPs in the last-hour logs. Query snapshot: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=ResourceName,AttributeValue=redwood-prod-01 --start-time 2024-04-18T02:00:00Z --end-time 2024-04-18T04:00:00Z` returned 48 decrypt events from 3 internal IPs.

Mike Chen: I'm running deeper checks on exported audit logs and will validate if any KMS decrypt requests originated from outside our VPCs. If anyone wants the quick grep I used: `zcat /tmp/ct-logs-2024-04-18.gz | jq '.Records[] | select(.eventName=="Decrypt") | .sourceIPAddress' | sort -u`. So far looks internal-only.

Leah Gomez: Draft customer advisory (first pass):

```
Subject: Notice: Security alert and precautionary action for encryption key used by Redwood services

Dear customer,

Today our security systems detected an anomalous pattern of decryption activity associated with an internal encryption key used by Redwood services. We immediately rotated the key and revoked the associated service credential as a precautionary measure. At this time, there is no evidence to date that any customer data has been accessed or exfiltrated.

What we did: rotated key, revoked credential, increased audit collection and monitoring, engaged incident response.

What you should know: there is no action required from you. If you have compliance or regulatory questions, contact security@redwood.ai.

We will provide updates if our investigation uncovers additional information.

Sincerely,
Redwood Security Team
```

Samir Patel: That looks good. Two technical clarifications to add: (1) the rotated key was a customer-agnostic internal signing key (not a per-customer KMS key), and (2) we are pushing extended audit exports for the last 90 days to S3 for post-incident review.

Priya Rao (Legal): Please change the phrasing "no evidence to date that any customer data has been accessed or exfiltrated" to "no evidence to date of customer data exfiltration" — short and avoids implying a complete absence of any access. Also confirm the contact alias `security@redwood.ai` is OK for regulated customers.

Leah Gomez: Updated draft with Priya's wording and added a short FAQ line about export availability. New draft: (see updated copy) — also added a requested timeline (04/18 02:58 UTC detection).

Jordan (CPO): Exec summary we can share with board and customers: 2-3 bullets: 1) detection + scope; 2) immediate containment actions (key rotate, credential revoke); 3) impact: no customer-facing impact identified; 4) follow-ups: extended audit + 72 hr enhanced monitoring + customer-facing note sent. Keep it high level.

Mike Chen: For operational steps, I recommend: (a) continue 24/7 log monitoring for 72 hours, (b) run a full IAM token issuance audit for svc-ingest-usw2, (c) push a read-only audit export to secure S3 for retention, (d) schedule a deeper memory dump/forensics on the affected host image if any sign of compromise surfaces.

Samir Patel: I will compile the exec one-pager now. Quick question — should we proactively offer customers their own audit export on request? That could trigger huge operational load. Thoughts?

Leah Gomez: Offer on-request only, with an intake form and a 48-72 hour SLA. We can prioritize regulated customers. Put that in the FAQ.

Priya Rao (Legal): Also recommend: do not promise timelines in customer emails beyond 'we will provide updates as available.' Keep it conservative.

Samir Patel: Updated final customer advisory posted below. Asking for sign-off to send at 19:00 PST (business hours) and to post to status.redwood.ai.

Samir Patel: Final customer advisory (ready to send):

```
Subject: Security notice: precautionary key rotation for Redwood services (04/18)

Hello,

Today we detected an anomalous pattern of decryption activity associated with an internal Redwood encryption key. As a precaution we rotated the key and revoked the associated service credential. There is no evidence to date of customer data exfiltration.

What we did:
- Rotated the internal key and revoked the implicated credential
- Increased audit logging and initiated extended exports for forensic review
- Implemented 72-hour enhanced monitoring on affected services

What you should know:
- No action required from customers
- Customers may request audit exports; we will handle requests through a review process

If you have questions, contact security@redwood.ai

Sincerely,
Redwood Security Team
```

Jordan (CPO): Read and approve. Good to go. Send at 19:00 PST. @Mike Chen coordinate throttle on the email send and status page post.

Mike Chen: Will do. I'll use the staged send with 1-minute rollouts and monitor bounces/errors. I'll also update the ticket with the status URL.

DevOps Bot: status.redwood.ai updated — incident notice published at 2024-04-18T19:00:00-07:00 (ID: st-2043).

Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. Post-incident follow-ups: add RBAC reviews for svc-ingest-usw2, ensure KMS usage alerts tuned, and add a retro in tomorrow's oncall sync.

Leah Gomez: I'll prepare a short external FAQ and a canned response for Support.

Priya Rao (Legal): Please route the final board note to me and to @Jordan for records.

Samir Patel: Filed. Closing thread for now, will reopen if new findings emerge. :white_check_mark:
